I emailed GOG once about the Galaxy client, and they responded within at least a day, but I can't say that makes me want to dive headfirst and cut Steam off entirely.

The main selling point for GOG is the lack of any DRM in their games. If - like me - you don't give a shit about DRM (not saying I agree, but I'm still playing the same game from whichever source), then you're only concern will be cost-of-games-related, which as you pointed out, is typically higher than Steam's. That said, I've got far more many games I've got for free from GOG (not only giveaways, but also for spending so much during their big, annual sales). They occasionally do beat out Steam though - I bought the STALKER games (and got STALKER CS free for spending so much and unlocking it), the price of which would never be seen on Steam. It's obviously anecdotal, but it does happen.

That said, GOG gives you a 30 day money back guarantee, whereas Steam is only offering a 14 day return tme, provided you haven't played more than 2 hours (in which case a refund isn't guaranteed).

Personally, I use both Steam and GOG. I tend to buy from just wherever's cheapest. Provided GOG Connect (import DRM free games from Steam library to GOG library) continues to rise in games added,
